guard: a port lost between pick and bind is retried on another port, within a bound, and a failure names what it tried
why: The recovery is the whole point, and three of its parts can rot independently: the retry itself,
the cleanup of the attempt that failed readiness, and what the give-up message carries. A suite that
only checked 'it eventually came up' would pass under a version that leaks a process per attempt and
under one whose failure names a single port — which is exactly how the original loss read as an
unhealthy runner rather than as a taken port.
The accept control is graded separately: an implementation that always retries would satisfy every
retry cell, so the one-attempt count on a free port is its own mutation.

mutations.name: readiness no longer decides, so the first attempt is always kept
mutations.find: if (await isUp(port)) return { started, port, attempts: attempt };
mutations.expectRed: a stolen port is retried, not fatal
mutations.cell: a stolen port is retried, not fatal
mutations.note: The pre-fix behaviour in one line: pick, start, hand it back. The accept control still passes, because a free port was always fine; only the stolen-port cell separates the two.

mutations.name: a failed attempt is left running
mutations.note: A spawned broker that started but never answered would survive every retry, so a suite that retries three times leaves two brokers behind. Invisible to any cell that only asks whether the run eventually succeeded.

mutations.name: the give-up message drops the ports it tried
mutations.expectRed: the failure names every port it tried
mutations.cell: the failure names every port it tried
mutations.note: One port in the message is how this defect read as an unhealthy runner for as long as it did: 45019 appeared exactly once in the whole job log.

mutations.name: a zero bound is accepted and silently does nothing
mutations.find: if (attempts < 1) throw new Error(`startOnFreePort: attempts must be at least 1, got ${attempts}`);
mutations.expectRed: a zero bound is refused, not silently treated as one
mutations.cell: a zero bound is refused, not silently treated as one
mutations.note: Without the refusal a caller passing 0 gets the give-up error with an empty list, which reads as 'nothing was free' rather than 'you asked for no attempts'.
